Every file & folder occupies ~150 bytes of JVM heap memory:
Non-volatile storage maintaining cluster state across restarts:
1. SNN fetches fsimage & edits via HTTP GET from NameNode.
2. Merges transactions in SNN memory ➔ Ships fsimage.ckpt back via HTTP POST.
128MB Chunks • Checksum Verification (CRC32C) • Zero-Copy Kernel Transfer
How Spark & MapReduce applications stream data directly into HDFS DataNode storage:
• Client connects to DataNode on port :9866
• Packets queued in dataQueue memory buffer
• Sends ACK packet upstream to client
🧱 Physical Storage Directory Layout on Docker Volume (hadoop_datanode_data):
• Exact binary payload of Parquet / CSV records
• Size on disk: Matches file size (not rounded to 128MB)
• Linux ext4 / XFS block storage filesystem
No padding waste • Zero storage bloat
• CRC32C checksums stored for every 512 bytes
DAG Scheduler • Task Sets • In-Memory RDD/DataFrame Cache • Port :8080
How Spark translates user queries into optimized physical stages:
Stage 0: Map / Partition Processing (Local to HDFS)
• Read HDFS CSV/Parquet blocks via hdfs://localhost:9000/...
• Row filtering, projection & map-side combine in RAM
• Write Snappy-compressed Parquet directly to HDFS
Event logs streamed to HDFS and surfaced on Spark History Server (:18080)
Standalone worker container connected via spark://spark-master:7077:
Zero Java GC overhead during large departmental aggregations.
Dynamic 3072MB Memory Pool • CapacityScheduler • NodeManager Slot Isolation
🧠 YARN Dynamic Container Scheduling Pool (3,072 MB Total)
512MB slot isolation ensures zero memory deadlocks across multi-tenant workloads:
🧠 NodeManager Enterprise Virtual Memory & GC Stability Tuning:
• vmem-check-enabled=false: Java 11/17 glibc threads allocate 64MB virtual memory arenas. Disabling vmem check prevents NodeManager from killing healthy containers.
• Low-Pause G1GC (-XX:+UseG1GC): Replaces outdated ParallelGC. Predictable pause targets (<200ms) prevent false container heartbeat timeouts during large job shuffles.
• MapReduce JobHistoryServer (JHS :19888): Preserves task counters, timeline data, and execution logs even after containers terminate.
• Cloud Storage Connector (CloudStorageFileSystem): On GCP Dataproc, containers stream directly to gs:// buckets with 11 9s durability and zero disk bottlenecks.
Verified Execution: Spark Monte Carlo Pi + PySpark HDFS Parquet ETL + MapReduce Pi Benchmark running in harmony.
Zero Data Loss: Named Docker Volumes, Spark Event Logs & Google Cloud Storage Buckets (gs://)
Filesystem namespace tree, fsimage snapshots, and edits WAL
Stores actual raw 128MB replicated data blocks (blk_* and blk_*.meta checksums)
Spark DAG event logs picked up by Spark History Server
MapReduce shuffle spills, intermediate buffers, and cloud staging
Durable PySpark notebooks, ETL pipelines, and dataset artifacts
